title: When the Alibi Sings
premise: When Sebastian Nakamura exhumes town founder Aldous Wren for a routine records dispute, the coffin is empty—and a brass ledger key sewn into the burial shroud points to a cipher hidden in the town's founding documents. As Sebastian decodes it, he learns Wren faked his death to expose the founding families' land-theft scheme, and that his own late mother was one of Wren's silent partners. The statute of limitations expires in thirty days, and someone on the town council will kill to keep the ledger buried. In the end, Sebastian publishes the decoded ledger at the founders' day ceremony, choosing truth over the loyalty that protected his family's name, and accepts that some graves must stay open.
about_author: Lena Vasquez is a former small-town newspaper reporter who spent a decade covering municipal corruption in rural Oregon before turning to fiction. She writes mysteries about the secrets communities keep to survive, drawing on her obsession with public records and the people who read them.

chapters.title: The Weight of Empty Ground
chapters.summary: Sebastian, POV throughout, supervises the court-ordered exhumation of Aldous Wren and finds the coffin empty except for a brass key stitched into the shroud. His pride in closing every case collides with dread as the judge demands answers within the month. Emotional beat: quiet professional confidence cracking into unease.

chapters.title: Every Grave by Name
chapters.summary: Sebastian reviews cemetery records and realizes Wren's plot was opened once before—fifteen years ago, the night Sebastian's mother died. A councilman, Harlan Pike, warns him off 'historical curiosities.' Emotional beat: the first hint that his own history is entangled with the crime.

chapters.title: A Ledger in Plain Sight
chapters.summary: Following the brass key's engraving, Sebastian discovers the cipher embedded in the numbered lots of the original town plat displayed in city hall. Decoded fragments reveal payments from founding families to unnamed recipients. Emotional beat: exhilaration of discovery shadowed by fear of what the names might be.

chapters.title: What Mother Kept
chapters.summary: In his mother's belongings, Sebastian finds matching cipher notes proving she was paid as Wren's courier—and that she died the week she tried to deliver the full ledger. POV shifts briefly to her old letters. Emotional beat: grief curdling into betrayal; loyalty to her memory now cuts both ways.

chapters.title: The Founding Families
chapters.summary: Sebastian quietly interviews the descendants of the four founding families, cataloguing alibis and inheritances. One descendant, Ruth Okafor, admits her grandfather confessed to burning Wren's real coffin—but not to moving the body. Emotional beat: mounting paranoia as each interview closes another door.

chapters.title: Fire at the Records Hall
chapters.summary: Arson destroys the county archive room holding Wren's death certificate. Sebastian saves a scorched fragment showing the body in the official coffin was never identified. Someone knows how close he is. Emotional beat: terror made concrete; the investigation turns dangerous.

chapters.title: Thirty Days, Twenty-Six Left
chapters.summary: With the statute clock ticking, Sebastian decodes the final section: the ledger names every bribe, including one signed by the current mayor's father. He realizes the killer must be someone with access to both the 1970s exhumation and today's council. Emotional beat: resolve hardening into strategy.

chapters.title: The Man Who Wasn't Buried
chapters.summary: Sebastian traces an unmarked pauper's grave to a man who lived under a false name until two years ago—Aldous Wren himself, alive long enough to hide the ledger's completion copy. At the grave he's ambushed by Harlan Pike, who confesses to the arson but claims the murder order came from above. Emotional beat: shock giving way to cold clarity.

chapters.title: Founders' Day
chapters.summary: Climax. At the founders' day ceremony, Sebastian publicly decodes the plat cipher before the assembled town, naming the families and revealing the mayor's father ordered Wren silenced and his mother killed. The mayor lunges; Ruth Okafor steps forward with the completion copy Wren left her family as insurance. Emotional beat: courage overtaking fear; truth spoken aloud.

chapters.title: Closing the Case
chapters.summary: Resolution. Arrests ripple through the council; the statute fight ends when prosecutors argue ongoing fraud tolls the clock. Sebastian reburial-plans Wren beside his mother's plot and finally inscribes a name on the empty grave: his own case closed, his invisibility surrendered. Emotional beat: bittersweet peace—truth cost him everything comfortable and gave him back himself.
